_comment: Independent-implementability ledger (SPEC §13). One record per blind
implementation attempt. This file is an ASSERTION about runs that happened;
scripts/check-implementability.py machine-checks the half that can be checked
— that each surface_digest is exactly what blind-export.py reproduces from the
recorded source — and enforces the structural rules §13 states. The verdict
itself is attested by the implementer and cannot be re-derived by CI, which is
why it carries the evidence pointer rather than standing alone.
Rounds are append-only. A superseded verdict is never edited: it is a fact
about a surface that existed, and later repair does not make it untrue.

rounds.surface_note: NOT RECORDED. This run predates blind-export.py and ran in a git worktree, so the supplied surface was not pinned by a manifest and cannot be reconstructed exactly. Per §13.3 the claim is therefore unbound, and is retained as history rather than as evidence.
inferred: the entire model lattice, reverse-engineered from vectors; the Apache-2.0 row was demonstrably free — all-UNSTATED, all-YES and all-NO each still passed 8/8
§12.4 encoding details not stated in that section
contamination: two commit SUBJECT LINES reached the agent's terminal via `git checkout` and `git log --oneline -1`; isolation was instructional rather than structural
part of §12 was repaired in 234e3ee between dispatch and return, so the run partly tested a document that no longer existed
rounds.implementer_statement: A reader with §12 and no fixtures cannot produce a single verdict. The vectors are functioning as normative text here.

inferred: `policy` — a required component of a normative identity with no vocabulary, default, semantics or stated source anywhere in the document; obtainable only by reading a fixture record, and BLOCKING: without the vectors no digest was producible at all
the source of `engine`
whether a member asserting nothing contributes an input pair
the tie-break when two pairs share a name
whether duplicate pairs are collapsed
the text encoding of the digest bytes, stated in §11.2 and §8.6.1 but not in §12.4
identifier matching discipline — literal, case-folded, or trimmed
the vector records' own schema, documented nowhere
contamination: the subject disclosed recognising this project from context available to it outside the task, and stated it did not consult that context; unremovable by the harness and the reason its clean first-run score is discounted
the subject wrote one file to the parent directory by mistake, moved it back, and ran `ls` there, seeing only `scratchpad` and `tasks`; no project content was exposed
rounds.implementer_statement: The claim under test — reproducible without inference — does not hold, principally because the `policy` field is a required component of a normative digest with no definition anywhere in the document.

inferred: `engine` — a required component of a normative identity with no vocabulary, default or stated source; the IDENTICAL defect repaired for `policy` one line above and not looked for in its sibling
sort DIRECTION — LICENSE-ORDER-INDEPENDENT names the sort keys and never says ascending; a descending implementation is prose-conformant and fixture-refuted
which key of model.json is the model version; the model file's SCHEMA is nowhere specified
a model row missing a dimension, or carrying a value outside {YES,NO,UNSTATED}
whether an unrecognised policy still computes a digest — resolved from a label in the non-normative matrix SCRIPT, disclosed as such by the subject
whether the character exclusion covers the header lines or only the triple
case sensitivity of the compound-operator test
whether uppercase hex in input-artifact/input-publication is rejected, case-folded, or encoded verbatim
how a `/1` envelope's no-assertion state joins to the `-` sentinel
the encoding for a member with no publication identity — NOT DETERMINED, and the reason two published vectors were irreproducible
the vector file's record schema
contamination: the subject's session context was injected with the project's CLAUDE.md and a memory index from outside the working directory; it did not seek them and could not decline them. It reports they contain no mention of licences, evaluation, grants, the lattice, or anything in §12 — recorded as a fact rather than weighed as a judgement

the subject read scripts/license-rule-matrix.py before the vector boundary (it is a named input) and discloses that its EXPECTED label for LICENSE-POLICY-DEFINED influenced one pre-boundary assumption
rounds.implementer_statement: A working implementation exists and reproduces 23 of 25 vectors on its first run. But several encoding details were not determined by the prose, and two fixtures are not reproducible from the specification at all.
rounds.constructive_note: On failing to reproduce two published fixtures the implementer searched over 160,000 candidate encodings, declined to infer the missing sentinel, and reported the fixtures as irreproducible rather than adjusting until they matched. 23/25 carrying that refusal is stronger evidence than 25/25 obtained by adaptation: it is the first round demonstrating resistance to teaching-to-the-test, and it is what exposed an undocumented constant in the reference.
